scenarios.name: tube-transfer
scenarios.purpose: Check a whole multi-leg Tube route; this example pair must be confirmed to yield a transfer in returned legs.

fareTo.purpose: Whole station-pair FareTo reference, not per-leg fare

scenarios.name: bus-plus-tube
scenarios.purpose: Mixed-mode case observed to include bus and Tube. FareTo checks only the Tube station pair, not the whole multimodal fare.

fareTo.purpose: Cross-check the Tube component only; never add this to the whole Journey Planner fare without confirming the scope

scenarios.name: consecutive-bus
scenarios.purpose: Candidate bus-only case; verify the returned route has multiple bus legs and inspect fare/Hopper fields. Do not treat each bus leg as a separately chargeable fare.

scenarios.name: rail-transfer
scenarios.purpose: Candidate National Rail case; verify the returned route includes a transfer and inspect its fare basis. FareTo support must be established from its actual response.

scenarios.name: osi-hammersmith
scenarios.purpose: Candidate route via the TfL-listed Hammersmith OSI. Confirm the returned route really interchanges between the paired Hammersmith stations; the API route is not a simulation of card taps.

fareTo.purpose: Whole rail-station-pair reference; check returned route options and fare caveats

scenarios.name: split-journey-reference
scenarios.purpose: Compare a continuous Charing Cross-to-Baker Street planner journey with two separately queried PAYG journey legs via Oxford Circus. Separate API requests do not emulate actual taps or prove a user's charged amount.

scenarios.name: zone-1-alternative
scenarios.purpose: Inspect candidate route options avoiding Zone 1 and their fare/tap fields. Journey Planner cannot simulate a passenger actually touching a pink reader; compare with TfL's Single Fare Finder and pink-reader guidance.

fareTo.purpose: Whole station-pair single-fare reference; inspect alternative route rows and caveats

scenarios.name: peak-boundary
scenarios.purpose: Compare same route on the same weekday around the published peak boundaries; observe returned chargeLevel, peak and offPeak rather than assuming boundary inclusivity.
